items.title: A fake E20 bandh, anchors off air, and a mystery yet to be solved
items.summary: Through the first week of July, Instagram reels began warning of a ‘Bharat Bandh’. Many were alarmist . Thumbnails urged people “not to step out of home”, said India was “on high alert”, and claimed public services would be disrupted on July 15. The shutdown, they said, was about E20 petrol. Many of these videos were by regional TV anchors – from Network18, TV9, News1 India, Zee News, News Nation and Bharat24 – posting from their personal handles, in the register they use on air. But there was no Bharat Bandh. No organisation had called one, not even the political parties that had been most vocal on E20. The channels’ editorial teams categorically denied issuing any instruction to this effect. At Network18, the reels had consequences. More than half-a-dozen regional anchors were temporarily taken off-air this July, sources said, and their phones were checked as part of an internal enquiry. According to one anchor who went through it, the enquiry also went through their ChatGPT histories. All the reels have now been deleted.
